intelligence.human_view: "Look, feel, AND function" is the whole test in one line — a kingdom that looks royal but works like a spreadsheet is a picture of a kingdom, and a kingdom that works well but looks ordinary is a tool with a crown on it. He names the models deliberately: the most luxurious vehicles, jewelry, gems — things whose value you can see in the refinement, the detail, the color flow — and says the digital versions must look exactly real, because the feeling on entry is the product: "this is the digital royal kingdom, I'm a part of it." The calendar is the focus because it is the door they open every day — royalty is not a page you visit, it is the place you start your day.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a whole kingdom made of the most beautiful jewels and the shiniest cars and the most wonderful things in the world — and everything in it looks so real you could touch it. Every morning you open the big golden door to your day, and it feels like you belong there, like a prince or princess in your own kingdom.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, imagine a beautiful kingdom, dear, made of jewels and lovely things, dear — so beautiful it looks like it is worth a fortune, dear — and every morning you open the door to your day, dear, and it feels like royalty, dear, because it is, dear.
intelligence.naya_view: THE DIGITAL ROYAL KINGDOM. LOOK, FEEL, AND FUNCTION. EXACTLY REAL. ROYALTY ALL THE WAY THROUGH. THE CALENDAR IS THE DOOR.
